newsitem.title: KYRGYZSTAN: Kyrgyzstan passes securities market programme.
newsitem.headline: Kyrgyzstan passes securities market programme.

text.p: Kyrgyzstan's government has adopted a three-year programme to develop the domestic securities market and attract local and foreign investors, a senior government official said on Friday.
"We hope to create by 1998 favourable conditions for investors and attract people's savings to the economy," Dzhon Dzhaparkulov, head of the State Securities Agency, told Reuters.
"Shares of foreign companies will be traded on the Kyrgyz secondary market, and Kyrgyz shares will be traded abroad."
Dzhaparkulov said that under the programme the government planned to attract savings of small private investors by issuing a state investment loan backed by shares of privatised companies.
Proceeds from the loan will be used to modernise these companies, he said.
The authorities also plan to abolish taxes on the revenues of local investment funds from operations on the securities market.

The securities market is currently controlled and regulated by the National Bank, the State Property Committee and two ministries, but in the near future will be coordinated by a single national securities commission accountable to the president.
"This will ensure investors' balance of interests," Dzhaparkulov said.
He said the programme toughened requirements for capital market participants and outlined rules for investment banks to ensure payments on operations with securities.
Dzhaparkulov said Kyrgyzstan had 1,300 joint-stock companies created through privatisation, and 25 companies were now listed on the Kyrgyz Stock Exchange.
